title: The Neoclouds Build Cash Hoards Faster Than Revenues
gist: A Q2 2026 read-through on the two public GPU neoclouds: CoreWeave carries a $104.2 billion backlog (plus $25 billion added since quarter-end), grew revenue 2.1X to $2.58 billion, spent $9.4 billion on capex and still exited with $6.41 billion of cash, while its net loss ballooned to $626 million against a near-breakeven $49 million operating loss; Nebius runs one-tenth CoreWeave's revenue on more than half its capex and has ratcheted contracted power from >1 GW to 5 GW in twelve months. Note a title/text discrepancy: the piece asserts cash hoards outgrowing revenues but never breaks out debt, prepayment structure or GPU depreciation schedules, so the funding mix behind the cash balances is implied rather than shown.

themes.theme: Neocloud origin story and structural position

insights.claim: GPU neoclouds were built recently and in some cases repurposed from cryptocurrency mining operations with the explicit strategy of undercutting hyperscaler pricing on GPU-accelerated GenAI training and inference capacity.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Price-undercutting is the whole business model, so neocloud gross margins are structurally capped by whatever the big clouds choose to charge — watch hyperscaler GPU list pricing as the ceiling on neocloud economics.
insights.quote: sometimes out of dubious cryptocurrency farms and explicitly to undercut the high prices that the big clouds can command for GPU-accelerated systems that support GenAI training and inference
insights.locator: The biggest clouds in the United States and China

insights.claim: Hyperscalers and frontier model builders including Anthropic and OpenAI are now buying capacity from the very neoclouds created to undercut them, meaning the largest cloud operators are simultaneously competitors and customers of the neocloud segment.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Neocloud revenue quality depends on customers who could in-source at any time; the arrangement persists only while supply is short, so treat these contracts as scarcity rents rather than durable share gains.
insights.quote: It is pretty funny when a big cloud buys capacity on a neocloud to support an AI model builder.
insights.locator: It is pretty funny when a big cloud

insights.claim: In the current AI compute market, competitive advantage reduces to who holds GPU or XPU allocations and what price they can extract, not to service differentiation or software stack quality.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Allocation access is the scarce asset to underwrite; a neocloud's supplier relationship, not its technology, is the moat to diligence.
insights.quote: it all comes down to who has the GPU or XPU allocations and what price they think they can get for access to them
insights.locator: But with the demand for compute being so much larger than supply

insights.claim: Most neocloud operators are private, so CoreWeave and Nebius are the only public windows into the segment's financial mechanics and function as bellwethers for the wider GPU-rental datacenter market.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Two disclosing names carry the read-through for an entire opaque asset class — their prints will move sentiment on private neocloud credit and on Nvidia channel demand well beyond their own float.
insights.quote: Few of the neoclouds are public companies, so we don’t get much insight into their inner workings.
insights.locator: Few of the neoclouds are public companies

insights.claim: CoreWeave has stated a near-term target that no single customer exceed 35 percent of its revenues, an implicit admission that its historical dependence on Microsoft was a concentration risk it is actively unwinding.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A 35 percent ceiling is still extreme concentration by normal credit standards — track disclosed customer mix each quarter as the key covenant-relevant metric for CoreWeave's debt.
insights.quote: wants no one company to have more than 35 percent of its revenues in the near term
insights.locator: It is not clear how dependent CoreWeave is currently on Microsoft

insights.claim: CoreWeave has signed long-term capacity deals worth $22.4 billion with OpenAI and $32 billion with Meta Platforms, plus agreements with Google and Anthropic, covering essentially every leading frontier model builder.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Two contracts alone total $54.4 billion; the counterparty credit of OpenAI and Meta is now effectively embedded in CoreWeave's enterprise value.
insights.locator: has inked long-term deals with OpenAI

insights.claim: Hedge fund Jane Street made a $1 billion strategic investment in CoreWeave, an equity stake that likely doubles as a commitment to rent CoreWeave capacity.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Quantitative finance entering GPU rental widens the demand pool beyond model builders — watch for other trading firms and banks signing capacity deals as a new demand vertical.
insights.locator: Hedge fund Jane Street

insights.claim: CoreWeave's revenue backlog reached $104.2 billion at the end of the June 2026 quarter and grew by a further $25 billion in roughly six weeks after quarter-end.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A backlog roughly 40X annualized Q2 revenue is the bull case and the risk in one number — conversion pace, not backlog size, is the metric that will re-rate or de-rate the stock.
insights.locator: Drilling down into the quarterly numbers

insights.claim: CoreWeave's June 2026 quarter revenue grew 2.1X year on year to $2.58 billion while capital expenditure in the same quarter was $9.4 billion, roughly 3.6 times revenue.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Spending 3.6X revenue on capex means external funding, not operations, drives the buildout — the equity story is levered to continued capital-market access.
insights.locator: In Q2, CoreWeave’s revenues grew by a factor of 2.1X

insights.claim: CoreWeave narrowed its quarterly operating loss to $49 million while its net loss expanded to $626 million, a roughly $577 million gap indicating that below-the-line financing and non-operating charges, not operations, now drive the company's losses.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The business is near operating breakeven but the capital structure is expensive — rising rates or wider credit spreads hit CoreWeave's bottom line far harder than any demand slowdown would.
insights.quote: it reduced its operating loss to $49 million, but the company’s net loss ballooned to $626 million
insights.locator: In Q2, CoreWeave’s revenues grew by a factor of 2.1X

insights.claim: CoreWeave ended the June 2026 quarter holding $6.41 billion in cash and equivalents, roughly 2.5 times its quarterly revenue, after already deploying $9.4 billion of capex in the period.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Cash balances rising faster than recognized revenue point to customer prepayments and debt draws pre-funding the next buildout — a liquidity cushion that is also a liability to the counterparties who supplied it.
insights.locator: The company spent $9.4 billion on capital expenses

themes.theme: Physical footprint and the power-to-GPU conversion

insights.claim: CoreWeave exited the June 2026 quarter with 51 datacenters and 1,500 MW of active installed power, which implies an estimated fleet of roughly 1.1 million GPUs.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Roughly 1.36 MW per thousand GPUs is a usable back-of-envelope conversion for sizing any operator's fleet from disclosed megawatts when GPU counts are undisclosed.
insights.quote: with 1,500 MW of active power installed, we reckon that this is around 1.1 million GPUs across its fleet
insights.locator: CoreWeave finished up Q2 with 51 datacenters

insights.claim: CoreWeave holds 3,700 MW of contracted power against 1,500 MW installed, meaning roughly 2,200 MW of committed capacity is still to be energized for model builders and Microsoft.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A 2.5X gap between contracted and live power is a forward order book for grid interconnects, transformers, cooling and Nvidia systems — read it as multi-year demand visibility for the power supply chain.
insights.locator: CoreWeave has 3,700 MW of contracted power

insights.claim: CoreWeave was the first company to bring up an Nvidia Vera-Rubin NVL72 system, doing so during the second quarter of 2026.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: First-to-deploy status on each Nvidia generation is CoreWeave's differentiator versus hyperscalers and a leading indicator of Vera-Rubin volume ramp timing.
insights.locator: Thanks to its tight relationship with Nvidia

insights.claim: Nvidia has deliberately cultivated the neoclouds as a competitive counterweight to hyperscalers that are designing their own CPUs and accelerators.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Neocloud allocations are a channel-strategy hedge against custom silicon; if hyperscaler in-house accelerators scale, expect Nvidia to push even more supply to neoclouds, sustaining their allocation edge.
insights.quote: which has been fostering the neoclouds to put competitive pressure on the big clouds who are all making their own CPUs and accelerators
insights.locator: Thanks to its tight relationship with Nvidia

insights.claim: Nebius, the Netherlands-based spinout of Russian internet conglomerate Yandex, generates roughly one-tenth of CoreWeave's revenue while spending a little more than half of CoreWeave's capital expenses, an extreme spend-to-revenue ratio aimed at capturing the 2027 GenAI systems opportunity.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Nebius is deliberately outspending its own revenue base by roughly 5X relative to CoreWeave — the highest-beta public expression of the view that 2027 GPU demand will absorb everything built.
insights.quote: Nebius has one-tenth the revenue but a little more than one half the capital expenses of CoreWeave
insights.locator: Nebius has one-tenth the revenue

insights.claim: Nebius carries just under $6 billion of deferred revenue against management claims of more than $40 billion in customer capacity commitments, a gap showing most of its pipeline is uncontracted or unbilled rather than prepaid.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Deferred revenue is the only cash-backed part of a commitment figure — the roughly 7X gap between the $40 billion headline and $6 billion deferred is the discount to apply to neocloud commitment announcements generally.
insights.locator: The company’s deferred revenue is, at just shy of $6 billion

insights.claim: Microsoft and Meta Platforms are widely believed to be Nebius's anchor customers although the company has not characterized its commitment base publicly.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: If true, both public neoclouds lean on the same two hyperscaler counterparties, so a single capex pause at Microsoft or Meta would hit the whole listed neocloud complex at once.
insights.quote: This has not been characterized, but it is widely believed that Microsoft and Meta Platforms are the anchor customers at Nebius.
insights.locator: The company’s deferred revenue is, at just shy of $6 billion

themes.theme: Nebius power ramp and shift to short-duration pricing

insights.claim: Nebius has raised its contracted-power guidance five times in twelve months, from more than 1 GW in August 2025 to more than 2.5 GW in November 2025, more than 3 GW in February 2026, more than 4 GW in May 2026 and 5 GW by the end of the June 2026 quarter.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A 5X guidance raise in a year is the cleanest public evidence that AI power demand is being revised upward faster than any planning cycle can absorb — a direct read-through to utilities, turbine and grid-equipment order books.
insights.locator: The interesting thing about Nebius is how its contracted power is growing

insights.claim: Nebius began signing short-term GPU capacity contracts of three to six months this quarter and told Wall Street it sees a price opportunity in the $40 million to $50 million per MW range, while its core business remains one-to-three-year contracts.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A spot-style tier appearing alongside long-term contracts is the first observable pricing signal in GPU rental — track whether that $40-50 million per MW range holds, since spot compression would arrive there before it shows up in backlog.
insights.quote: price opportunity in the $40 million to $50 million per MW range
insights.locator: This quarter, Nebius started inking short-term contract deals
